newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: FOCUS-Sri Lanka to upgrade oil facilities.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Sri Lanka to upgrade oil facilities.

text.p: Sri Lanka plans to upgrade and expand its oil facilities over the next few years to cope with increasing demand for oil products, the head of state oil company Ceylon Petroleum Corp (CPC) said on Wednesday.

CPC Chairman Anil Obeyesekere said consumption for oil products was rising rapidly in the Indian Ocean island due to an expansion of industry and burgeoning demand for diesel as a source of power and for fuel for vehicles.
"Estimates are that there is a 10-15 percent growth rate (per year) in the consumption of diesel due to thermal power and due to the increased transport activity," Obeyesekere said in an interview.

He said Sri Lanka would import around 691,000 tonnes of diesel this year, up from 592,000 in 1996 and diesel imports would rise to 720,000 tonnes in 1998. By 2000, diesel demand would be around 150 percent of 1996 levels, he said.
Sri Lanka used to rely on hydropower for much of its electricity needs but a series of droughts in recent year highlighted the need to look for other sources of power.
